content: Fluocinonide is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It may also be used for other purposes as directed by your doctor. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Fluocinonide is available in different forms, including ointment, cream, solution, and gel, and in various strengths for application on the skin. Typically, it is applied two to four times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use fluocinonide exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid applying it to other areas of your body or covering the treated area with wraps or bandages unless instructed to do so by your doctor. Before applying the medication, wash or soak the affected area thoroughly unless doing so irritates your skin. Apply a thin layer of the ointment, cream, solution, or gel sparingly and rub it in gently. If using the solution or gel on your scalp, part your hair, apply a small amount to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Protect the treated area from washing or rubbing until the solution or gel dries. You may wash your hair as usual, but not immediately after applying the medication. Avoid prolonged use of fluocinonide on the face, genital and rectal areas, skin creases, or armpits unless directed by your doctor. If applying it to your face, ensure it does not come into contact with your eyes. If using it on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as this may increase side effects. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin preparations to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: Wash or soak the area thoroughly. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected areas. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). You may use plastic gloves for hands, plastic bags for feet, or a shower cap for the scalp. Seal the edges of the plastic wrap carefully to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partly unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. Leave the plastic wrapping in place for the duration instructed by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrapping is applied. Contact your doctor if the treated area worsens or if you experience burning, swelling, or oozing of pus. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using fluocinonide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluocinonide or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using fluocinonide, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Fluocinonide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Itching Burning Changes in skin color If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Skin infection (redness, swelling, or oozing pus) If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store fluocinonide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat, and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly, and do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
